newsitem.title: GERMANY: German overnight call money eases to 3.08-3.12 pct.
newsitem.headline: German overnight call money eases to 3.08-3.12 pct.

text.p: German call rates were slightly easier on Tuesday morning at between 3.08 percent and 3.12 percent in relaxed dealings.

Traders said they expected call rates to remain around current levels in the afternoon and that the Bundesbank may add a small amount in Wednesday's repo allocation when 72.7 billion marks of repos is set to expire.
Any net add the Bundesbank makes on Wednesday, however, may be offset when a 3.2 billion mark, five-day tender set last Friday expires.
Banks held 45.9 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Monday, leaving the average for the month so far at 41.1 billion marks.
Only around 200 million marks was borrowed from the Bundesbank's 4.5 percent emergency Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered rate stood at 3.09045 Tuesday morning, down from 3.12767 percent the day before.
